prompts.wave: Use case: identity-preserve / game animation sprites. Reference image: the EXISTING orange Claude/Clawd eight-state atlas provided. Preserve EXACT character identity: wide terracotta-orange rectangular slab body with subtle beveled top/left edges, two simple tall black rectangular eyes, four small stubby rectangular feet, two small square block hands on short flexible orange arms. No mouth, no cheeks, no clothes, no new facial features. Create ONE production sprite sheet for a COMPLETE HAND-WAVING action, not a character redesign. Crisp high-detail pixel art suitable for a native 128x128 sprite, limited terracotta palette, dark burnt-orange outlines, warm highlights, minimal texture. Transparent background, no glow or backdrop, no ground shadow, no particles, no lettering, no frame lines. EXACTLY 8 frames in a strict 4 columns by 2 rows grid, equally sized square cells, row-major chronological order. Every cell uses identical camera, scale, body proportions and a fixed floor baseline 85% down the cell; generous transparent margins and no artwork may touch another cell. The body must keep the same dimensions across frames. Frame 1: neutral front-facing body, both arms relaxed. Frame 2: right elbow bends, right hand lifts to side of body. Frame 3: right hand raised above upper-right corner, palm/block rotates outward. Frame 4: wave fully outward, right arm extended. Frame 5: wave inward, elbow bent, block hand rotates inward. Frame 6: a second outward wave, eyes briefly blink to thin slits. Frame 7: hand lowers towards side. Frame 8: neutral body matching frame 1. The other hand and four feet keep a stable stance. Each frame must visibly change actual arm shape, elbow bend and hand orientation; do not simulate waving by translating or resizing the whole character. This is the same original Claude character animated, with subtle charm, not a new mascot. Output a square 1024x1024 sheet with strict 4x2 layout.
prompts.typing: Use case: identity-preserve / animation game sprites. Image 1 is the original Claude/Clawd character and its working pose with three chunky gray keyboard keys. Image 2 is the approved waving sheet and sets the exact new pixel-art character style to match. Create a NEW TYPING action sheet for the SAME orange Clawd. Invariants: wide terracotta rectangular slab body with beveled top/left, two tall black rectangle eyes, four short block feet, small square orange hand blocks with flexible short orange arms; NO mouth, no clothes, no cheeks, no antennae, do not redesign. Match body size, orange palette and dark burnt-orange outlines of image 2. Render as detailed crisp pixel art for a 128x128 game sprite. EXACTLY 8 chronological frames in strict 4 columns x 2 rows square cells on a square 1024x1024 canvas. Transparent background, no glow, no shadow, no background, no labels, no gridlines, no effects. Each frame centered in its equal cell, identical camera and scale, feet baseline 85% down its cell; ample transparent separation. Three chunky light-gray keycaps form the keyboard in front of the four feet, like original working pose, and remain fixed across all frames. Animate real elbow bends, hand rotation and keycap depression, NOT whole-body movement. Frame1 both square hands poised over keys. Frame2 left elbow bends and left hand rises while right hand presses right key. Frame3 left hand swings down and depresses left key while right hand lifts. Frame4 left key releases, left hand rises and right hand presses middle key. Frame5 both hands briefly hover, eyes focused on keyboard. Frame6 left hand presses middle key while right hand raises high. Frame7 right hand swings down to depress right key, left hand returns to hover. Frame8 return to frame1 for seamless typing loop. Keep the rectangular body fixed and same proportions while arms and hands articulate in clearly different poses. The keyboard must be the SAME object, no typing screen or extra props.
prompts.jump: Use case: identity-preserve / game sprite animation. Image 1 is original orange Claude/Clawd, image 2 is the approved same-character pixel-art sheet. Create a new COMPLETE CELEBRATORY JUMP sequence using this EXACT character. Preserve the terracotta rectangular slab with beveled top/left edges, the simple tall black rectangle eyes (can become inverted-V happy eyes in the air), four short rectangular feet and two small square orange hand blocks on flexible orange arms. NO mouth, no clothes, no new details. Match image 2 body dimensions, outlines and palette. Detailed crisp pixel art for a 128x128 sprite. EXACTLY 8 frames in a STRICT 4 columns x 2 rows grid on square 1024x1024 transparent canvas. Each equal square cell uses the SAME centerline, camera and scale, fixed imaginary ground at 85% down the cell, leaving a lot of space above for jump. Transparent background with no shadows, no confetti, no motion lines, no lettering, no labels, no grid. The body is roughly 60% of the cell width, not oversized. Frames row-major: 1 neutral stance feet planted arms down; 2 anticipation: four feet bend and spread, knees visibly tucked, body crouches lower, arms swing backwards; 3 takeoff: feet push down and straighten, arms swing outwards/up, body just lifting; 4 ascent: body clearly airborne HIGH above ground, feet tucked towards body, both elbows bent with hands over upper corners, happy inverted-V eyes; 5 apex: highest position, both arms reach fully up with square hands above body, feet splay outward, happy eyes; 6 descent: body lower, feet extend down preparing for landing, elbows lower halfway; 7 landing: feet contact ground and bend/spread, hands drop to sides, low crouched position; 8 recovery: return to same neutral stance as frame1. Real changes to foot bend, arm articulation and body elevation. No mere whole-image squash/scale. Keep physical body width and height consistent, only legitimate foreshortening during the crouch. No overlapping neighboring cells.
